parsed.why: No criminalisation; highest court has ruled for trans interests (bathroom, surgery mandate). Friction is bathhouse guidance and family-register custody for detainees, plus no anti-discrimination statute. Reserved but non-hostile society; rule of law works for trans people.

Recent decriminalisation with a court extending constitutional sex-discrimination protection to gender identity; no trans-specific offence or targeting documented. Thin record: no protection statute, no recognition mechanism, no documented social acceptance — extrapolated to moderate, not hostile.

No criminalisation, but acceptance of 5/100, a 2024 report documenting torture, sexual violence and extortion, death threats against the sole trans public figure from legislators, police inaction, no protection statute and ambiguous hate-crime cover: hostility with thin recourse.

Active morality-law enforcement: 84 arrested incl. trans women in a four-month sweep, upheld convictions to 4.5 years, forced anal examinations, systemic birth-name/birth-sex processing in detention. State-directed targeting of gender-nonconforming people with no protection machinery.

Gender identity is a statutory protected ground with hate-speech and penalty provisions — but enforcement is uneven, 222 hate incidents in one year, physical attacks on a gender-nonconforming person, and Pride needing 2,000 police: protections exist but hostility is documented at scale.
